RFC 9162 Section 5 gives these messages in prose and ships no JSON Schema. INSTANCE: the decoded GET query string as a JSON object of strings (Section 5: order-independent key/value URL parameters). start and end are 0-based decimal indices (Section 5.6). start <= end is a MUST (rfc-9162#R-0081) that a schema cannot state: ../messages.yaml, MSG-28. Instances are JSON values as received; binary fields stay base64 text and are not decoded (RFC 4648 Section 4, per Section 5). A pattern ^AQ[...] on a TransItem field binds the first two decoded octets, the VersionedTransType code of Section 4.5, because base64 of 0x01 0x0T begins AQ (every code here has 0 in its high nibble) and the low nibble T confines the third character to a block of four, its other two bits coming from the next octet; hence four characters per code in each pattern. The pattern states what a v2 log emits; it is not a client acceptance test, since a v2 client MUST NOT construe a non-v2 SCT (rfc-9162#R-0069) or an unrecognized TransItem type (rfc-9162#R-0079) as an error. Fields the RFC does not define are allowed (Section 5: any fields not understood SHOULD be ignored). A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. This schema cannot check the TransItem body, signatures, or any cross-field relation: those are in ../messages.yaml (constrained_by and notes per field).
